name: a header and two rows: two records in a fresh anonymous array, Count 2, Changed
Has Header off: rows of cells, plain nested arrays, every cell a string; '' on it is off too
a byte-order mark is stripped, \r\n ends a row, and a trailing newline is a trailing row with one empty cell (a short row leaves its missing column undefined)
because: csv.ts :78-80 stripBOM; :32-34 the trailing-row behaviour carried over; :195-199

name: an unpaired quote fails with the line it gave up on, leaving Items and Count as they were: Error, Failure, no Changed; the next good parse clears Error (the wire keeps the sentence)
an unpaired quote at the very end of the text is the other half of the verdict: the scanner stops with input left
';' and a tab parse a European export and a TSV; a Delimiter cleared to '' reads as ','
because: parsecsv.ts :109 `value || ','`; csv.ts :107-118 the pattern is built from the delimiter

name: three inputs in one frame parse once: one Changed, under the delimiter that arrived last
because: parsecsv.ts :166-175 _schedule's guard — the reason a graph that sets Delimiter and CSV together does not parse with the old delimiter first

name: an empty quoted cell is '' (not undefined), a doubled quote is one quote, a short row leaves its missing columns undefined
because: csv.ts :36-43 the one behaviour changed; :131 `!== undefined`

name: null is not an arrival (nothing, not even Failure); a number parses as its text — a header-only file yields no records, Count 0, Changed
because: parsecsv.ts :85 textSupplied; :179; csv.ts :165 String(text); :194 header-only → no records

name: a second successful parse replaces Items with a FRESH array — its name on the wire moves — and the records inside are minted anew
because: parsecsv.ts :201 Collection.get() with no name every parse; NSP-012 AC6 the $array wire form
